Conspiracy is an inchoate offense that requires proof of:

  • an agreement
  • between two or more persons
  • to accomplish an unlawful purpose
  • with the specific intent to accomplish that purpose.

A hub-and-spoke conspiracy is one in which the co-conspirators (the spokes) do not know of each other and instead transact individually with a central actor (the hub). Essentially, the "hub" commits several isolated conspiracies with each "spoke." The hub is liable for the conspiracies with each of the spokes, but the individual spokes are not liable for the acts of each other.

Here, the employee (the hub) embezzled rare game pieces then separately agreed with various individuals (the spokes) to receive a percentage of the cash prizes they received. While the employee would be liable for each isolated conspiracy with each of the individuals, the defendants were also charged with entering into a single conspiracy. And because the individuals transacted individually with the employee and did not know of the other individuals' participation in the scheme, the defendants cannot be properly convicted of the single conspiracy.

(Choices A and C) Although only the employee embezzled the game pieces from the retailer, the individuals committed false pretenses by falsely stating that they had obtained all of the necessary game pieces through authorized, legitimate channels. And here, the defendants conspired to commit false pretenses by entering into separate agreements with the employee to obtain money from the retailer by such means. But the defendants cannot be convicted under a single conspiracy, as they were a part of several isolated conspiracies.

(Choice D) Each individual did share 50 percent of the prize received from the retailer with the employee. However, the various individuals were unaware of each other, and each individual entered into a separate, isolated conspiracy with the employee. So the defendants cannot be convicted of entering into a single conspiracy.

📌 Educational Objective

In a hub-and-spoke conspiracy, the hub (the central actor) is liable for the conspiracies with each of the spokes (the co-conspirators), but the individual spokes are not liable for the acts of each other.
questions.zh-question:
一家零售商赞助了一项游戏，要求个人收集游戏碎片以赢取各种现金奖品。该零售商的一名员工侵吞了赢取高额现金奖品所需的稀有游戏碎片。该员工随后分别联系了多名个人，并向每人提供了一块稀有游戏碎片。该员工没有透露，这些个人也不知道，该员工还向其他人提供了游戏碎片。随后，每名个人都将必要的游戏碎片（包括该员工提供的稀有碎片）提交给零售商以换取现金奖品。为了获得奖品，每名个人都虚假声称自己是通过授权的、合法的渠道获得了所有游戏碎片。收到奖金后，每名个人都按照事先约定，将奖金的50%支付给了该员工。
除其他罪名外，该员工和所有个人都被指控犯有单一的“串谋以虚假借口（false pretenses）从零售商处获取金钱”罪。
被告们能否被恰当地定罪为该串谋罪？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为只有该员工侵吞了零售商的游戏碎片。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为这些个人并不知道其他个人参与了该计划。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为每名个人都虚假声称自己是通过授权的、合法的渠道获得了所有必要的游戏碎片。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为每名个人都与该员工分享了从零售商处获得的奖金的50%。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑法与程序: 未遂犯与共犯

正确答案: B

不能，因为各个人员（轮辐）不知道其他人员（轮辐）参与了该计划，因此不能构成一个单一的阴谋罪。

核心法律原则

阴谋罪 (Conspiracy)

阴谋罪的构成要素

阴谋罪 (Conspiracy) 是一种未遂犯 (inchoate offense)，需要证明以下要素：

  • 存在一项协议 (agreement)；
  • 在两人或多人 (two or more persons) 之间；
  • 旨在实现一个非法目的 (unlawful purpose)；
  • 并具有实现该目的的特定意图 (specific intent)。

轮辐式阴谋罪 (Hub-and-spoke conspiracy)

轮辐式阴谋罪的特点与责任

在轮辐式阴谋罪 (Hub-and-spoke conspiracy) 中，共同谋划者（通常称为轮辐，spokes）彼此之间互不相识，而是各自与一个中心行为人（轮轴，hub）单独进行交易。本质上，“轮轴”与每个“轮辐”分别构成了数个独立的阴谋罪。

在这种结构下，轮轴对与每个轮辐的阴谋罪负责，但各个轮辐不对其他轮辐的行为负责，因为他们之间缺乏直接的协议或相互认知，无法构成一个单一的、整体的阴谋。

概念对比：链式阴谋罪 vs. 轮辐式阴谋罪

特征 链式阴谋罪 (Chain Conspiracy) 轮辐式阴谋罪 (Hub-and-spoke Conspiracy)
结构 参与者形成一个线性链条，每个成员都与链条中的相邻成员有联系，并且通常知道整个链条的存在和目的。 一个中心人物（轮轴）与多个独立人物（轮辐）分别达成协议，轮辐之间互不相识。
相互认知 通常，每个成员都知道其他成员的存在和参与，或者至少知道他们的行为是为了实现一个共同的、更大的目标。 轮辐之间彼此不知道对方的存在或参与。
责任范围 所有共谋者通常对其他共谋者的行为负责，因为他们被视为一个单一的、整体的阴谋的一部分。 轮轴对与每个轮辐的阴谋罪负责。但各个轮辐不对其他轮辐的行为负责，因为他们之间没有直接的协议或相互认知。

案情分析与法律适用

本案中，零售商的员工（轮轴，hub）从零售商处侵吞了稀有游戏碎片，然后分别 (separately) 联系了多名个人（轮辐，spokes），并向他们提供了游戏碎片。员工没有透露，且这些个人也不知道其他任何人参与了该计划。

虽然员工与每个个人之间都存在一项协议，旨在通过虚假陈述（false pretenses）从零售商处获取金钱，并且每个个人都与员工分享了奖金，但这些个人（轮辐）之间并没有彼此达成协议，也没有相互了解对方的参与。

因此，这构成了一个典型的轮辐式阴谋罪。在这种结构中，轮轴（员工）与每个轮辐（个人）之间存在独立的阴谋罪，但各个轮辐之间不构成一个单一的、整体的阴谋罪，因为他们之间缺乏相互的协议和认知。

要证明存在一个单一的阴谋罪，必须证明所有被指控的共谋者都同意了同一个非法目的，并且通常需要他们之间有某种程度的相互认知或理解，即他们是更大计划的一部分。本案中，轮辐之间缺乏这种相互认知。

图示：轮辐式阴谋罪

轮辐式阴谋罪 (Hub-and-spoke Conspiracy)

轮辐共谋者不对其他轮辐共谋者的行为负责。

陷阱警示

MBE 考试中常见的陷阱是混淆链式阴谋罪 (Chain Conspiracy) 和轮辐式阴谋罪 (Hub-and-spoke Conspiracy)。

  • 在链式阴谋罪中，即使成员之间不直接认识，但如果他们知道或应该知道他们的行为是为实现一个更大的、共同的非法目标所必需的，那么他们可能被视为一个单一阴谋的一部分，并对其他共谋者的行为负责。
  • 在轮辐式阴谋罪中，轮辐之间缺乏这种相互认知和共同的整体目标，因此他们通常不能被视为一个单一阴谋的成员，也不对其他轮辐的行为负责。

关键在于轮辐之间是否存在相互认知和共同的整体目标。

正确答案与干扰项排除

B. 不能，因为各个人员不知道其他人员参与了该计划。

正确。 本案是一个典型的轮辐式阴谋罪 (hub-and-spoke conspiracy)。员工是“轮轴”，而各个个人是“轮辐”。尽管每个“轮辐”都与“轮轴”达成了协议，但“轮辐”之间彼此互不相识，也不知道其他“轮辐”的存在。因此，他们之间缺乏构成一个单一阴谋罪所需的相互协议和认知。他们可以被指控与员工分别构成阴谋罪，但不能被指控构成一个涵盖所有“轮辐”的单一阴谋罪。

A. 不能，因为只有员工侵吞了零售商的游戏碎片。

错误。 尽管只有员工实施了侵吞行为，但各个个人也通过虚假陈述（false pretenses）从零售商处获取了金钱，并与员工分享了收益。他们各自与员工达成了非法协议，因此他们也参与了犯罪。然而，这并不是他们不能被指控构成一个单一阴谋罪的主要原因。主要原因是他们之间缺乏相互认知。

C. 能，因为每个个人都虚假陈述称其通过授权的合法渠道获得了所有必要的游戏碎片。

错误。 尽管每个个人都实施了虚假陈述，这确实是犯罪行为（例如，构成虚假陈述罪或与员工构成阴谋罪），但这本身并不能证明所有个人之间存在一个单一的阴谋罪。缺乏轮辐之间的相互认知是关键障碍。

D. 能，因为每个个人都与员工分享了从零售商处获得的奖金的50%。

错误。 个人与员工分享奖金是他们与员工之间存在协议的证据，也是他们非法目的的一部分。但这并不能弥补各个个人之间缺乏相互认知和协议的缺陷，从而无法构成一个涵盖所有人的单一阴谋罪。

考试技巧

在 MBE 考试中，当遇到多个犯罪分子与一个中心人物互动，但彼此之间互不相识的情况时，要警惕这可能是一个轮辐式阴谋罪 (hub-and-spoke conspiracy)。在这种情况下，通常不能指控所有“轮辐”构成一个单一的、整体的阴谋罪，因为他们之间缺乏必要的相互协议和认知。

记住：轮辐之间没有相互责任。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
In a jurisdiction that has abolished the felony-murder rule but otherwise follows the common law of murder, a husband and wife, both armed with automatic weapons, went into a bank to rob it. The husband ordered all the persons in the bank to lie on the floor. When some were slow to obey, the wife, not intending to hit anyone, fired about 15 rounds into the air. One of these ricocheted off a stone column and struck and killed a customer in the bank.
The husband and wife were charged with murder of the customer.
Which of the following is correct?

choices.A: Both can be convicted of murder.
choices.B: Neither can be guilty of murder, but both can be convicted of manslaughter based upon an unintentional homicide.
choices.C: The wife can be convicted of murder, because she did the act of killing, but the husband cannot be convicted of either murder or manslaughter.
choices.D: The wife can be convicted only of manslaughter, but the husband cannot be convicted of murder or manslaughter.

questions.explanation:
A defendant is guilty of common-law murder if she unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought, which encompasses the following mental states:

  • Intent to kill
  • Intent to inflict serious bodily harm
  • Reckless disregard of a high risk of serious bodily injury or death (i.e., depraved-heart murder)
  • Intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony (i.e., felony murder)—abolished in this jurisdiction

A principal is the person whose acts or omissions are the actus reus of the crime—i.e., the perpetrator of the crime. And an accomplice is a person who intentionally aids or abets the principal prior to or during the commission of the crime. An accomplice is responsible for the targeted crime to the same extent as the principal. And if the principal commits crimes other than the crime the accomplice encouraged or assisted, then the accomplice is liable for those other crimes that are the natural and probable consequences of the accomplice's conduct.

Here, the wife committed murder when she recklessly disregarded the high risk to human life posed by shooting 15 rounds into the air inside the bank (malice aforethought) and killed a bank customer (unlawful killing). The husband is also guilty of murder as an accomplice because (1) he aided his wife with the armed bank robbery and (2) the murder was a natural and probable consequence since they used automatic weapons (Choice C). Therefore, both can be convicted of murder.

(Choices B and D) The husband and wife may be guilty of involuntary manslaughter—i.e., an unintentional killing caused by an unlawful act or criminal negligence. But since the wife killed the customer with malice aforethought (recklessness) and the husband was her accomplice, they can be convicted of the more serious crime of murder.

📌 Educational Objective

Common-law murder is an unlawful killing with malice aforethought (e.g., depraved-heart murder). And an accomplice—one who intentionally aids or abets a principal—can be convicted of the targeted crime and any crimes that are the natural and probable consequences of the accomplice's conduct.
questions.zh-question:
在一个已经废除了 felony-murder rule 但在其他方面遵循谋杀罪普通法的司法管辖区，一对夫妻均持有自动武器进入一家银行实施抢劫。丈夫命令银行内的所有人趴在地上。当一些人迟缓未从时，妻子无意击中任何人，向空中开了约15枪。其中一颗子弹从石柱上反弹，击中并杀死了一名银行顾客。

这对夫妻被控谋杀该顾客。

以下哪项陈述是正确的？

zh-choices.A: 两人均可被判谋杀罪。
zh-choices.B: 两人均不构成谋杀罪，但均可因非故意杀人行为而被判过失杀人罪。
zh-choices.C: 妻子可被判谋杀罪，因为是她实施了杀人行为，但丈夫不能被判谋杀罪或过失杀人罪。
zh-choices.D: 妻子只能被判过失杀人罪，但丈夫不能被判谋杀罪或过失杀人罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Inchoate Crimes & Murder

✅ 正确答案：A (两人均可被判谋杀罪)

这道题是一个经典的刑法陷阱题，考察了在没有重罪谋杀规则 (Felony-Murder Rule) 的情况下，如何认定谋杀罪以及共犯责任。

考点一：废弃心谋杀

题目明确指出该司法管辖区废除了 Felony-Murder Rule。这意味着我们不能仅仅因为他们在抢劫中导致他人死亡就直接判定谋杀。

我们需要回到普通法谋杀的核心要素：预谋恶意 (Malice Aforethought)。预谋恶意不仅包含杀人意图，还包含：

  • 意图造成严重身体伤害
  • 废弃心/极端鲁莽 (Depraved Heart / Reckless Indifference to Human Life)
💡 案例分析：
妻子在狭窄的银行空间内，手持自动武器向空中连开15枪。虽然她没有杀人意图（Intent to kill），但这种行为对他人生命构成了极高风险，且她对此表现出鲁莽的无视。这符合 Depraved Heart Murder 的定义。
考点二：共犯责任

丈夫没有开枪，为什么也要承担谋杀罪责？这里考察的是共犯责任 (Accomplice Liability)。

根据普通法，共犯不仅对目标犯罪（抢劫）负责，还对主犯实施的、作为目标犯罪自然且可能之后果 (Natural and Probable Consequences) 的其他犯罪负责。

  • 丈夫协助了持械抢劫（目标犯罪）。
  • 在持械抢劫中，同伙开枪导致他人死亡是完全可预见的 (Foreseeable)。

因此，丈夫必须为妻子构成的 Depraved Heart Murder 承担责任。

为什么其他选项错误？

❌ 选项 B & D (过失杀人 Manslaughter)：
过失杀人通常适用于“刑事过失” (Criminal Negligence) 或“激怒杀人” (Provocation)。但在本案中，在银行内乱射自动武器的行为危险程度极高，超过了普通过失，上升到了“恶意” (Malice) 的层面，因此构成谋杀而非过失杀人。

❌ 选项 C (丈夫无罪)：
这忽略了共犯责任中的“可预见性”原则。只要死亡是持械抢劫的可预见后果，共犯就难逃其咎。

🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
当题目说“Felony-Murder Rule 被废除”时，不要立刻排除谋杀罪。出题人通常是在测试你是否能识别出 Depraved Heart Murder（极端鲁莽导致的谋杀）。只要行为极度危险（如乱开枪、向人群扔石头），即使没有杀意，也是谋杀。

A.text: Both can be convicted of murder

B.text: Neither can be guilty of murder

reason.zh: 错误地将无杀人故意视为否定所有谋杀理论的依据。

B.text: manslaughter based upon an unintentional homicide

reason.en: Understates the culpability; depraved-heart recklessness elevates the offense to murder.
reason.zh: 低估了罪责；无视人命的鲁莽行为应升级为谋杀罪。

C.text: husband cannot be convicted of either murder or manslaughter

reason.en: Ignores that husband aided the robbery with weapons, making murder a natural and probable consequence.
reason.zh: 忽视了丈夫持武器协助抢劫，谋杀为自然且可能的后果。

D.text: wife can be convicted only of manslaughter

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A bank teller was fired by the president of the bank. The teller decided to take revenge against the president but decided against attempting it personally because he knew the president was protected around the clock by bank security guards. The teller also knew that his cousin had a violent temper and was very jealous. The teller falsely told his cousin that the cousin's wife was having an affair with the president. Enraged, the cousin said, "What am I going to do?" The teller said, "If it were my wife, I'd just march into his office and blow his brains out."
The cousin grabbed a revolver and rushed to the bank. He walked into the bank, carrying the gun in his hand. One of the security guards, believing a holdup was about to occur, shot and killed the cousin.
If the teller is charged with attempted murder of the president, which verdict should be rendered?

choices.A: Guilty, because he intended to kill the president and used the cousin to carry out his plan.
choices.B: Guilty, because he was extremely reckless as to the president.
choices.C: Not guilty, because the cousin, if successful, would be guilty of no more than manslaughter and an accomplice cannot be guilty of a higher crime than the principal.
choices.D: Not guilty, because the president was never in imminent danger of being killed.

questions.explanation:
Malice aforethought (attempted v. completed murder)
Attempted
murder
Completed
murder
Intent to kill Conscious desire for, or substantial
certainty of, death
Intent to inflict serious bodily injury Conscious desire for, or substantial certainty of,
serious bodily harm
Depraved-heart murder Reckless disregard for high risk of death
or serious bodily harm
Felony murder Killing during
inherently
dangerous felony

Attempt is an inchoate crime that requires proof of three elements:

  • The defendant had the specific intent to commit a crime.
  • The defendant—or his/her agent—performed an act in furtherance of that crime.
  • The target crime was not completed.

Proof of specific intent is always required for attempt—even when proof of a lesser mental state would be sufficient for the target crime. Therefore, a defendant is only guilty of attempted murder if he/she specifically intended to kill the victim. No other type of malice aforethought will suffice (Choice B).

Here, the teller intended to have the bank president killed. And the teller committed an act in furtherance of this crime—and used the cousin to carry out his plan—when the teller lied to the cousin about his wife's affair and urged him to shoot the president. But since the cousin was shot by a security guard, the president's murder was never completed. Therefore, the teller is guilty of attempted murder.

(Choice C) Had the intended murder been successful, it would not have been reduced to voluntary manslaughter since there was no adequate provocation or other mitigating factor. And though an accomplice (person encouraging crime) cannot be guilty of a higher crime than the principal (person committing criminal act), they are equally liable. Therefore, the teller (accomplice) and the cousin (principal) are equally guilty of attempted murder.

(Choice D) The lack of imminent danger would only negate the act requirement in the few jurisdictions that use the dangerous proximity test. Under this test, an act occurs when the defendant is so close to completing the target crime that it is essentially unstoppable. But most jurisdictions use the substantial step test, which only requires that an act exceed mere preparation and strongly corroborate the defendant's criminal intent.

📌 Educational Objective

Attempt always requires (1) the specific intent to commit a crime and (2) an act by the defendant or his/her agent in furtherance of that crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名银行出纳员被银行行长解雇。该出纳员决定向行长复仇，但他决定不亲自下手，因为他知道行长受到银行保安24小时的保护。该出纳员还知道他的表亲脾气暴躁且非常善妒。该出纳员向其表亲谎称，表亲的妻子与行长有染。表亲勃然大怒，说道：“我该怎么办？”出纳员说：“如果那是我妻子，我就会直接冲进他的办公室，一枪打爆他的头。”

表亲抓起一把左轮手枪冲向银行。他走进银行，手里拿着枪。一名保安以为即将发生抢劫，开枪打死了表亲。

如果该出纳员被控谋杀行长未遂，应作出何种裁决？

zh-choices.A: 有罪，因为他意图杀害行长，并利用其表亲来执行他的计划。
zh-choices.B: 有罪，因为他对行长的安危表现出极端鲁莽。
zh-choices.C: 无罪，因为其表亲即使成功，也最多构成非预谋杀人罪，而从犯的罪名不能比主犯更重。
zh-choices.D: 无罪，因为行长从未处于即将被杀害的迫在眉睫的危险之中。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 刑法考点解析

未遂犯 (Attempt) 与 间接正犯
正确答案：A 有罪。因为出纳员具有杀害行长的特定意图，并利用其表亲作为工具（Agent）来实施该计划。
考点一：未遂罪的特定意图

Attempt (未遂) 是典型的“不完整罪” (Inchoate Crime)。在普通法和大多数司法管辖区，未遂罪必须证明两个要素：

  • Specific Intent (特定意图)：被告必须明确意图实施目标罪行。
  • Overt Act (公开行为)：实施了超越单纯预备的实质性步骤。

⚠️ 关键点： 即使目标罪行（如谋杀）可以通过“鲁莽” (Recklessness) 定罪，但谋杀未遂 (Attempted Murder) 必须要求有杀人的特定意图。

考点二：间接正犯 / 无辜代理人

本题的核心在于Innocent/Unwitting Agent (无辜/不知情代理人) 理论。

当被告利用他人作为工具来实施犯罪时：

  • 如果被利用者（表亲）不知情、被欺骗或无犯罪意图，法律将利用者的行为直接归责于被告。
  • 被告被视为一级主犯 (Principal in the First Degree)，就像他亲手扣动扳机一样。

在本案中，出纳员通过谎言激怒表亲，将表亲变成了“人肉武器”。表亲持枪冲进银行的行为（Overt Act），在法律上被视为出纳员的行为。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 B (错误)： 提到“极端鲁莽” (Extremely Reckless)。
虽然鲁莽足以构成“Depraved Heart Murder”（如果受害人死亡），但不足以构成谋杀未遂。未遂必须是 Specific Intent。
选项 C (错误)： 提到“从犯不能重于主犯”。
首先，出纳员是间接正犯而非从犯。其次，即使表亲因“激情杀人”仅构成非预谋杀人 (Manslaughter)，出纳员也不能借此减责。出纳员是冷静策划的，没有受到法律认可的挑衅 (Provocation)，因此他具备谋杀的恶意 (Malice)。
选项 D (错误)： 提到“没有迫在眉睫的危险”。
大多数辖区采用Substantial Step Test (实质性步骤测试)。表亲持枪进入银行已经构成了实质性步骤，无需等到最后一刻。
🎓 MBE 答题技巧：

看到“借刀杀人”的情节（利用小孩、精神病人、或被欺骗的人），要立即联想到 Innocent Agent 理论。

此时，幕后操纵者不是“教唆犯”或“从犯”，而是主犯 (Principal)。被利用者的行为就是主犯的行为。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A construction company sent a bill to a customer who had hired the company to do work on the customer's home. The bill contained charges for material and labor for construction that was done on the personal residence of the company's president, rather than the customer's home. The customer paid the bill, believing it was for his home. Subsequently, the company and its president were charged with the crime of conspiring to commit theft as well as the crime of theft. The customer lived in the state that was prosecuting these crimes. The company was incorporated in another state and its president lived in that state. Each defendant was convicted of both crimes.
The theft crime is statutorily defined as follows: "A person commits the offense of theft if the person obtains property of another by deception." The conspiracy crime is statutorily defined as follows: "A person commits the offense of conspiracy to commit theft when the person agrees with another to commit theft of any property that belongs to another." Both crimes include a legal entity within the definition of "person."
The company and its president have appealed their convictions for the conspiracy offense only. Which of the following is their best defense to this crime?

choices.A: A corporation cannot be criminally liable because it cannot form the requisite mens rea.
choices.B: The company and its president are a single entity for purposes of this crime.
choices.C: The crime of conspiracy to commit theft merges into the completed crime of theft.
choices.D: The state lacks the authority to prosecute this crime.

questions.explanation:
Conspiracy
Agreement Overt act
Majority view
(modern & MPC)		 Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement At least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view
(common law)		 Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement Not required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Common-law conspiracy is (1) an agreement between two or more persons to commit a crime that is (2) entered with the specific intent to accomplish that crime. This bilateral approach requires proof of at least two guilty minds (i.e., plurality of agreement). Similarly, this jurisdiction statutorily defines conspiracy to commit theft as:

  • an agreement
  • with another person (including a legal entity (e.g., corporation))
  • to commit theft (i.e., obtaining property of another by deception)
  • of any property that belongs to another.

In some jurisdictions, there cannot be a conspiracy between a corporation and a single agent of that corporation. But in most jurisdictions, a conspiracy between a corporation and multiple agents of the same corporation may satisfy the plurality requirement.

Here, the construction company and its president have appealed their convictions for conspiracy to commit theft. This jurisdiction requires the agreement of two people. And though the company is considered a “person” in this jurisdiction, only a conspiracy between the corporation and multiple agents satisfies the plurality requirement. Therefore, the best defense to the crime of conspiracy is that the company and its president are a single entity for the purpose of this crime.

(Choice A) A corporation can form the requisite mens rea required for conspiracy. This is because a corporation may be held vicariously liable for the acts of its agents.

(Choice C) While inchoate crimes such as attempt and solicitation merge into the completed crime, the crime of conspiracy does not.

(Choice D) A state may prosecute an out-of-state defendant for conspiracy if he commits an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy within the prosecuting state. And here, though the defendants resided in another state, sending the bill to the customer in the prosecuting state constituted such an overt act.

📌 Educational Objective

In some jurisdictions, no conspiracy can exist between a corporation and a single agent. But in most jurisdictions, a conspiracy can exist between a corporation and multiple agents of the same corporation.
questions.zh-question:
一家建筑公司向一位客户寄送了一份账单，该客户曾雇佣该公司在其家中进行施工。该账单包含的材料和人工费用，是为公司总裁的私人住宅而非客户家中进行的施工。客户支付了账单，误以为是为自己家中的施工付费。随后，该公司及其总裁被控犯有共谋盗窃罪 (conspiracy to commit theft) 和盗窃罪 (theft)。客户居住在起诉这些罪行的州。该公司在另一个州注册成立，其总裁也居住在该州。每位被告均被判两项罪名成立。
盗窃罪的法定定义如下：“任何人通过欺骗手段获取他人财产，即构成盗窃罪。” 共谋罪的法定定义如下：“任何人与他人合谋盗窃属于他人的任何财产，即构成共谋盗窃罪。” 这两项罪名中，“人”的定义均包含法律实体。
该公司及其总裁仅对共谋罪的定罪提出上诉。以下哪项是他们对此罪名的最佳辩护？

zh-choices.A: 公司不能承担刑事责任，因为它无法形成必要的犯罪意图 (mens rea)。
zh-choices.B: 就本罪而言，公司及其总裁是一个单一实体。
zh-choices.C: 共谋盗窃罪 (conspiracy to commit theft) 合并到已完成的盗窃罪 (theft) 中。
zh-choices.D: 该州缺乏起诉此罪的权限。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑法与程序法: 未遂犯与共犯

正确答案: B
公司及其总裁就本罪而言是单一实体。

核心法律规则

共谋罪 (Conspiracy) 的复数要求

共谋罪是一种未遂犯（inchoate crime），通常要求：(1) 两人或两人以上之间的协议（agreement between two or more persons）；(2) 具有实施犯罪的特定意图（specific intent）。

在普通法共谋罪（common-law conspiracy）中，通常采用双边方法（bilateral approach），即要求至少有两名具有犯罪意图的人（guilty minds）达成协议。这被称为“复数要求”（plurality requirement）。

关于法人（corporation）与代理人（agent）之间的共谋，不同司法管辖区有不同规定：

  • 在某些司法管辖区，公司与其单一代理人之间不能构成共谋，因为他们被视为单一实体，无法满足复数要求。
  • 但在大多数司法管辖区，公司与其多名代理人之间可以构成共谋，满足复数要求。

本案中的司法管辖区明确规定，虽然公司被视为“人”，但只有公司与“多名代理人”之间的共谋才能满足复数要求。因此，公司与其单一总裁被视为单一实体，无法满足共谋罪的复数要求。

概念比较：共谋罪的不同观点

观点 协议 (Agreement) 实施行为 (Overt Act)
多数观点 (现代法与MPC) 单边方法 – 至少一人明确意图达成协议 至少一名共谋者必须实施实施行为
少数观点 (普通法) 双边方法 – 两人或两人以上明确意图达成协议 不要求

MPC = 模范刑法典 (Model Penal Code)

案情分析与法律适用

1. 识别罪名: 建筑公司及其总裁因共谋盗窃罪（conspiracy to commit theft）和盗窃罪（theft）被定罪，但他们仅对共谋罪提出上诉。

2. 共谋罪的定义: 本司法管辖区将共谋罪定义为“与他人达成协议以实施盗窃”。盗窃罪定义为“通过欺骗手段获取他人财产”。“人”的定义包括法律实体（legal entity）。

3. 复数要求: 根据本司法管辖区的规定，共谋罪要求“两人”之间的协议。虽然公司被视为“人”，但本司法管辖区进一步明确，只有公司与“多名代理人”之间的共谋才能满足复数要求。

4. 本案事实: 本案的共谋方是公司和其唯一的总裁。总裁作为公司的单一代理人。

5. 法律适用: 由于本司法管辖区要求公司与“多名代理人”才能满足共谋罪的复数要求，而公司和其总裁（单一代理人）被视为单一实体，因此他们之间的协议不满足共谋罪的复数要求。这是他们最好的辩护理由。

图示：共谋罪的复数要求（本司法管辖区）

公司 (Corporation)
↓ (单一代理人)
总裁 (President)
↓
视为单一实体
↓
不满足本司法管辖区的复数要求 (2人)

本司法管辖区要求
↓ (构成共谋)
公司 + 多名代理人
↓
满足复数要求

考点陷阱提示

在处理涉及公司及其代理人的共谋罪问题时，务必注意司法管辖区的具体规定。有些司法管辖区可能允许公司与单一代理人之间构成共谋，而另一些（如本案）则坚持“复数要求”，认为公司与单一代理人构成单一实体，无法满足共谋的“两人”要求。这是MBE常考的细微差别。

正确答案与干扰项排除

B. 公司及其总裁就本罪而言是单一实体。

本司法管辖区采用普通法共谋罪的双边方法，要求至少有两名具有犯罪意图的人。虽然公司被视为“人”，但本司法管辖区规定，只有公司与“多名代理人”之间的共谋才能满足复数要求。公司及其总裁（单一代理人）被视为单一实体，因此不满足共谋罪的“两人”要求。这是他们最好的辩护理由。

A. 公司不能承担刑事责任，因为它不能形成必要的犯罪意图（mens rea）。

这是一个普遍错误的陈述。公司可以通过其代理人的行为形成必要的犯罪意图（mens rea），并承担刑事责任。因此，这不是一个有效的辩护。

C. 共谋盗窃罪已并入已完成的盗窃罪。

共谋罪通常不并入已完成的犯罪。这意味着被告可以因共谋罪和已完成的犯罪分别被定罪和惩罚。只有像未遂（attempt）和教唆（solicitation）这样的未遂犯才会并入已完成的犯罪。

D. 该州缺乏起诉本罪的权力。

如果共谋的实施行为（overt act）发生在该州境内，即使被告居住在其他州，该州也有权起诉。本案中，公司向客户发送账单（构成实施行为）发生在该州，因此该州有权起诉。

备考锦囊

在MBE中，当题目涉及公司共谋时，请特别关注司法管辖区对“复数要求”的解释。区分公司与单一代理人、公司与多名代理人之间的共谋是否满足“两人”或“多方”协议的要求是关键。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A boyfriend approached a hitman and inquired about hiring someone to kill his girlfriend's parents. Unknown to the boyfriend, the hitman was an undercover police officer who pretended to agree to handle the job and secretly taped subsequent conversations with the boyfriend concerning plans and payment.
A few days before the payment was due, the boyfriend changed his mind and called the plan off. Nevertheless, the boyfriend was charged with solicitation to commit murder.
Should the boyfriend be acquitted or convicted of solicitation, as defined at common law?

choices.A: Acquitted, because he withdrew before payment and commission of the act.
choices.B: Acquitted, because no substantial acts were performed.
choices.C: Convicted, because the "hitman" agreed to commit the offense.
choices.D: Convicted, because the offense was completed before his attempt to withdraw.

questions.explanation:
Defenses unique to solicitation
Impossibility
  • Legal – when solicited act would not be criminal if completed
  • Factual – no defense
Withdrawal /
Renunciation
  • Majority/common law – no defense
  • Minority/MPC – when solicitor voluntarily renounces & thwarts commission
    of solicited crime
Exemption from
solicited crime
  • Not guilty of solicited crime if legislature intended to protect solicitor
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Solicitation is an inchoate crime that occurs when a person (1) entices or encourages another to commit a crime (2) with the specific intent that the solicited crime be committed. Solicitation is completed—regardless of whether the solicited party agrees to commit the crime or takes any step toward doing so—once these elements are met. Therefore, a complete and voluntary renunciation of one's criminal purpose (ie, withdrawal) is no defense to solicitation in common law (and most other) jurisdictions.

Here, the boyfriend's solicitation was complete the moment he inquired about hiring someone to kill his girlfriend's parents—regardless of whether the "hitman" agreed to handle the job (Choice C). And though the boyfriend later changed his mind and called off the plan before the hitman had been paid or committed the murder, withdrawal is no defense (Choice A). As a result, the boyfriend should be convicted of solicitation to commit murder.

(Choice B) Solicitation does not require a substantial act. Instead, this offense is complete the moment a person entices or encourages another to commit a crime with the requisite intent.

📌 Educational Objective

Solicitation is complete once a person entices or encourages another to commit a crime with the specific intent that the crime be committed. And at common law (and in most jurisdictions), withdrawal is no defense.

一名男友联系了一名杀手，询问雇人杀害其女友父母的事宜。该男友不知道的是，这名杀手是一名卧底警察，他假装同意接下这桩差事，并秘密录下了后续与该男友关于计划和报酬的对话。

在付款到期前几天，该男友改变了主意，并取消了计划。尽管如此，该男友仍被控教唆谋杀罪。

根据普通法（common law）对教唆罪的定义，该男友应被宣告无罪还是被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 宣告无罪，因为他在付款和实施犯罪行为之前撤回了。
zh-choices.B: 宣告无罪，因为没有实施任何实质性行为。
zh-choices.C: 定罪，因为“杀手”同意实施该罪行。
zh-choices.D: 定罪，因为在他试图撤回之前，罪行已经完成。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑法：教唆罪与撤回抗辩

✅ 正确答案：D 定罪，因为在他试图撤回之前，罪行已经完成。
Convicted, because the offense was completed before his attempt to withdraw.
⚖️ 核心法律规则
教唆罪 (Solicitation) 的定义

在普通法（Common Law）下，教唆罪包含两个要素：

  1. 引诱或鼓励他人犯罪（Inciting, counseling, advising, urging, or commanding another to commit a crime）；
  2. 具有特定的意图（Specific Intent），即希望被教唆的罪行得以实施。

关键点：罪行的完成时间

教唆罪是一种举动犯。当你把“请求”说出口的那一刻，罪行就已经完成（Completed）了。

  • 不需要对方同意（如果对方同意，可能构成共谋罪 Conspiracy）。
  • 不需要对方实施任何犯罪行为。
  • 不需要对方采取任何实质性步骤。
🔍 深度解析：为什么选 D？

本题考察的是撤回（Withdrawal/Renunciation）是否构成教唆罪的抗辩理由。

普通法规则 (Common Law Rule)

在普通法下，撤回不是教唆罪的抗辩理由。

因为教唆罪在“开口请求”的那一瞬间已经既遂。你不能“撤回”一个已经完成的犯罪。虽然男友后来改变了主意，但这只能说明他不想继续推进谋杀，无法抹去他已经实施了“教唆”这一犯罪事实。

因此，选项 D 正确指出：在他试图撤回之前，教唆罪已经完成。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 A (Acquitted/Withdrawal)：这是最大的陷阱。虽然在《模范刑法典》（Model Penal Code, MPC）下，如果自愿放弃并成功阻止罪行发生，可能构成抗辩；但题目明确问的是普通法（Common Law）。在普通法下，撤回无效。
  • 选项 B (No substantial acts)：混淆了未遂罪（Attempt）与教唆罪。未遂罪确实需要“实质性步骤”（Substantial Step），但教唆罪只需要“动嘴”即可，不需要实施实质性行为。
  • 选项 C (Hitman agreed)：教唆罪的成立不依赖于被教唆者的同意。即使杀手当场拒绝，男友依然构成教唆罪。如果杀手同意了，两人可能构成共谋罪（Conspiracy），但这并不是定罪教唆的前提。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

遇到 Solicitation（教唆） 的题目，请立即检查以下两点：
  1. 适用法律：题目问的是 Common Law 还是 MPC？（Common Law 不允许撤回抗辩；MPC 允许）。
  2. 罪行合并 (Merger)：如果被教唆的罪行真的完成了，教唆罪通常会“合并”进主罪（Substantive Crime）。但在本题中，谋杀未发生，所以只定教唆罪。
MBE Legal Analysis | Inchoate Crimes

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
While on their way home from a ball game, a driver and his passenger stopped at an all-night gas station. The passenger offered to pay for the gas. While the passenger pumped gas, he was surprised to see the driver enter the station, take money from the unattended cash drawer, and get back in the car. The passenger paid the attendant for the gas, and the driver drove off. The driver offered to reimburse the passenger for the gas, but the passenger declined. After discovering the missing cash, the gas station attendant called the police, and the driver was later stopped. The driver escaped with the stolen money, however, and was never prosecuted.
If the passenger is prosecuted for theft as an accomplice, should he be convicted?

choices.A: No, because he had no intent to promote the commission of the offense.
choices.B: No, because the driver, the principal, was never prosecuted.
choices.C: Yes, because he facilitated commission of the offense by failing to make any effort to stop it.
choices.D: Yes, because he paid the attendant while he knew the driver was holding the stolen money.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
(modern & majority approach)
Party Definition Liability
Principal
  • Commits criminal act with requisite mens rea or
  • Tricks or forces another (ie, innocent agent) to commit criminal act
 Liable for resulting crime
Accomplice
  • Aids or encourages principal before or during crime with intent that principal commit crime
 Liable to same extent as principal
Accessory
after the fact
  • Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction
 Liable for independent crime (not principal's)

An accomplice is someone who (1) intentionally aids or encourages another (the principal) before or during a crime (2) with the intent that the crime be completed—making both parties equally liable for the crime. Since the passenger was surprised to see the driver steal the money and had no intent to help the driver do so, the passenger should not be convicted of theft as an accomplice.

(Choice B) In most jurisdictions, an accomplice can be convicted of a crime even if the principal was never prosecuted for (or convicted of) the crime. Therefore, the fact that the driver (principal) was never prosecuted does not preclude the passenger's conviction. Nevertheless, the passenger should not be convicted of theft as an accomplice because he did not intend to help the driver complete the crime.

(Choices C & D) Although the passenger made no effort to stop the driver's theft and paid the attendant while knowing that the driver had taken the money, neither of these facts shows that the passenger had the mental state necessary to trigger accomplice liability (ie, that he intended to promote the theft).

📌 Educational Objective

Accomplice liability arises when a person (1) intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime (2) with the intent that the crime be completed. Both parties are then equally liable for the crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名司机和他的乘客在看完球赛回家的路上，停在了一家通宵营业的加油站。乘客主动提出支付油费。当乘客加油时，他惊讶地看到司机进入加油站，从无人看管的收银机里拿走钱，然后回到车上。乘客向服务员支付了油费，然后司机开车离开。司机提出要补偿乘客的油费，但乘客拒绝了。加油站服务员发现现金丢失后报了警，司机随后被拦下。然而，司机带着偷来的钱逃脱了，并且从未被起诉。

如果乘客作为盗窃罪的从犯被起诉，他是否应被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不应定罪，因为他没有意图促成该罪行的实施。
zh-choices.B: 不应定罪，因为司机，即主犯，从未被起诉。
zh-choices.C: 应定罪，因为他没有做出任何努力来阻止罪行，从而为罪行的实施提供了便利。
zh-choices.D: 应定罪，因为他在明知司机持有被盗钱款的情况下，仍然向服务员付款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑法：从犯责任 (Accomplice Liability)
⚖️ 核心法则：双重意图 (Dual Intent) 要确立从犯责任 (Accomplice Liability)，被告必须具备以下两个心理状态 (Mens Rea)：
  1. 意图帮助主犯 (Intent to assist the principal)；以及
  2. 意图促成该犯罪行为的实施 (Intent that the offense be committed)。
✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 A)

本题的正确答案是 A。

关键事实：题目明确指出乘客看到司机偷钱时感到“惊讶 (surprised)”。

法律推理：

  • 缺乏意图：由于乘客对司机的行为感到惊讶，证明他在盗窃发生前或发生时，并没有“促成犯罪实施”的意图 (Specific Intent)。
  • 从犯的定义：仅仅在现场或者事后知情，不足以构成从犯。从犯必须在犯罪完成之前，带着促进犯罪的目的去提供帮助或鼓励。

因此，因为乘客没有促成盗窃的意图 (Mens Rea)，他不能被定罪为盗窃罪的从犯。

❌ 干扰项辨析

选项 B 关于主犯未被起诉

错误原因：在普通法 (Common Law) 中，从犯的定罪确实依赖于主犯的定罪。但在现代法律（以及 MBE 采用的主流规则）中，即使主犯被无罪释放、未被起诉或享有豁免权，从犯仍然可以被独立定罪。因此，司机未被起诉不是乘客脱罪的理由。

选项 C 关于未阻止犯罪

错误原因：一般而言，旁观者没有法律义务去阻止犯罪 (No duty to act)。单纯的“不作为” (Mere presence or failure to intervene) 并不构成协助或教唆，除非被告对此负有特定的法律义务（如警察或保安），而本题中乘客只是普通路人。

选项 D 关于事后付款

错误原因：这是一个典型的陷阱。

  • 乘客虽然支付了油费，这可能帮助了司机逃跑，但这发生在盗窃行为（拿钱）已经完成之后。
  • 如果在犯罪完成后提供帮助以逃避抓捕，这构成的罪名是事后从犯 (Accessory After the Fact)，这是一个独立的罪名，而不是盗窃罪本身的从犯 (Accomplice to Theft)。
  • 题目问的是“作为盗窃罪的从犯 (Accomplice)”，因此该选项错误。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理共犯 (Parties to Crime) 题目时，请务必区分：

  • Accomplice (从犯)： 发生在犯罪前或进行中，目的是让犯罪成功。责任 = 与主犯相同。
  • Accessory After the Fact (事后从犯)： 发生在犯罪后，目的是帮主犯逃避法律制裁。责任 = 较轻的独立罪行。

本题中乘客的行为更接近“事后从犯”（如果他有帮助逃跑的意图），但他绝不是盗窃罪的“从犯”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man who owned a failing construction business lacked the money and supplies necessary to complete a major industrial project. In order to acquire supplies for the major project, the man planned to take supplies that another client had purchased and delivered for the construction of an apartment complex. The man shared his plan with a friend, an employee of the construction business, and asked the friend to help him retrieve the supplies from the business's storage facility. The friend knew that the supplies belonged to the other client but nevertheless agreed to help the man. Unbeknownst to the man and the friend, the apartment project had recently been canceled and the supplies had been returned to the client.
The next day, the friend went to the storage facility to get the supplies. The friend searched the facility for only a few minutes when he had a change of heart and left. However, his movement around the facility had triggered a silent alarm that turned on the surveillance cameras and alerted the police.
The friend and the man were later arrested, charged with conspiracy to commit larceny, and tried separately. The man was acquitted based on a lack of evidence, but the friend's trial is still pending.
In a jurisdiction that follows the modern-prevailing approach for conspiracy, is the friend likely guilty?

choices.A: No, because the friend's subsequent withdrawal from the conspiracy prevented its success.
choices.B: No, because the man was acquitted due to insufficient evidence.
choices.C: Yes, because impossibility is not a defense to conspiracy.
choices.D: Yes, because the friend agreed to take the supplies and committed an overt act.

questions.explanation:
Conspiracy
Agreement Overt act
Majority view
(modern & MPC) 		Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement At least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view
(common law) 		Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement Not required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

In most jurisdictions (including this one) and under the MPC, conspiracy requires proof of the following:

  • two or more persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to accomplish an unlawful purpose (e.g., larceny) and
  • at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.

And since these jurisdictions follow the unilateral approach, a conspiracy may be formed when only one party actually agrees and, for example, the other party merely feigns agreement.

Here, the friend entered an agreement to commit larceny when he agreed to help the man take another client's supplies and use them for a different project. The friend then committed an overt act in furtherance of this agreement when he went to the storage facility to retrieve the supplies. As a result, the friend is likely guilty of conspiracy to commit larceny.

(Choice A) Under the MPC and the minority view, subsequent withdrawal is a defense to conspiracy if the defendant voluntarily acts to "thwart the success" of the conspiracy. But in most jurisdictions, withdrawal is a defense only if it occurs before an overt act has been committed. Here, the friend committed an overt act when he went to the storage facility, so his subsequent change of heart is no defense.

(Choice B) The fact that the man was acquitted of conspiracy in a previous trial does not affect the friend's guilt because unilateral-approach jurisdictions require proof of only one guilty mind. Therefore, a jury is not precluded from finding the friend guilty of conspiracy to commit larceny in his separate trial.

(Choices C) Impossibility is a defense to conspiracy if the object of the agreement is not a crime. But it is not a defense when, as here, an unknown condition (e.g., return of the supplies) prevents the completion of the intended crime.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the modern-prevailing view, conspiracy requires proof that (1) one party actually entered an agreement with the specific intent to accomplish an unlawful purpose and (2) at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.
questions.zh-question:
一个经营着一家濒临倒闭的建筑公司的男子，缺乏完成一个大型工业项目所需的资金和物资。为了给这个大型项目获取物资，该男子计划拿走另一位客户为建造一个公寓大楼而购买并已送达的物资。该男子将他的计划告诉了他的一位朋友，这位朋友是该建筑公司的雇员，并请求这位朋友帮助他从公司的仓库中取回这些物资。这位朋友知道这些物资属于另一位客户，但还是同意帮助该男子。该男子和他的朋友都不知道的是，公寓项目最近已被取消，物资也已退还给客户。

第二天，这位朋友去了仓库取物资。这位朋友在仓库里搜寻了几分钟后，改变了主意并离开了。然而，他在仓库内的活动触发了一个静默警报，该警报启动了监控摄像头并通知了警方。

这位朋友和该男子后来被捕，被指控共谋实施盗窃罪（conspiracy to commit larceny），并被分别审判。该男子因证据不足被宣告无罪，但这位朋友的审判仍在进行中。

在一个遵循现代主流共谋罪立场的司法管辖区，这位朋友是否有罪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为这位朋友后来退出共谋，阻止了共谋的成功。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该男子因证据不足被宣告无罪。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为“不能犯”不是共谋罪的抗辩理由。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为这位朋友同意拿走物资并实施了一个显性行为（overt act）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 刑法考点解析

Inchoate Crimes: Conspiracy (共谋罪)
正确答案：D 是，因为这位朋友同意拿走物资并实施了一个显性行为 (overt act)。
⚖️ 法律规则：现代共谋罪

本题考察的是现代主流观点 (Modern-Prevailing Approach) 下的共谋罪构成要件。这通常参考《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code, MPC)。

共谋罪的两大核心要素：
  1. 合意 (Agreement)： 两人或多人达成实施非法行为的协议。
  2. 显性行为 (Overt Act)： 至少有一名共谋者为了推进该协议实施了某种公开行为（哪怕是准备工作）。

题目明确指出该司法管辖区遵循“现代主流观点”。这有两个关键推论：

比较维度 普通法 (Common Law) 现代/MPC (Modern)
合意理论 双方理论 (Bilateral)
必须两人都真心同意。如果一人是卧底，另一人无罪。		 单方理论 (Unilateral)
只要被告有犯罪意图并达成协议即可，哪怕对方是假装的或后来被无罪释放。
显性行为 通常不需要 必须有
(Overt Act)
🔍 案情涵摄 (Application)

让我们将规则应用到本案事实中：

  • 合意： 朋友“同意帮助该男子”去取物资。尽管物资属于他人，但他明知并同意了。这满足了 Agreement 和 Intent。
  • 显性行为： 朋友“去了仓库”并“搜寻了几分钟”。这不仅仅是思想，而是为了推进犯罪实施的具体行动。这满足了 Overt Act。

结论： 一旦实施了显性行为，共谋罪即告成立 (Completed)。后续的放弃或失败不影响共谋罪本身的成立。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A：关于“退出” (Withdrawal)

虽然朋友后来改变主意离开了，但在大多数司法管辖区，一旦显性行为发生，共谋罪已经完成，此时退出不能作为对“共谋罪”本身的抗辩（可能可以作为后续实体犯罪的抗辩）。
即使在允许退出作为抗辩的少数规则下（如MPC），通常要求被告采取行动成功阻止犯罪发生。这里朋友只是自己走了，并没有阻止犯罪（犯罪没成是因为物资不在，而不是因为他走了）。

选项 B：关于“同伙无罪” (Acquittal of Co-conspirator)

这是单方理论 (Unilateral Approach) 的考点。在现代规则下，不需要两个人都被定罪。只要被告（朋友）有犯罪意图，即使同伙（男子）因证据不足被释放，也不影响对被告的定罪。

选项 C：关于“不能犯” (Impossibility)

物资已经被退还，导致盗窃在事实上不可能完成（Factual Impossibility）。但这从来不是共谋罪的有效抗辩。只要他们认为可以偷，并达成了协议，共谋就成立了。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

遇到共谋罪 (Conspiracy) 题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 看前缀： 题目问的是 Common Law 还是 Modern/MPC？
    • 如果是 Modern，适用单方理论（一人有罪即可）+ 需要显性行为。
    • 如果是 Common Law，适用双方理论（两人必须都真心同意）+ 通常不需要显性行为。
  2. 找行为： 只要迈出了实质性的一步（如去现场、买工具），共谋罪通常就锁定了 (Locked in)。
  3. 忽略结果： 犯罪是否成功、东西是否在场，通常不影响共谋罪的成立。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man wanted to kill his coworker because the man believed the coworker was having an affair with the man's wife. Early one morning, armed with a pistol, the man crouched behind some bushes on a park hillside overlooking a path upon which the coworker frequently jogged. On this morning, however, the man saw the coworker jogging on another path about a half mile away. Nonetheless, the man fired five shots at the coworker. None of the five shots came anywhere close to the coworker as he was well out of the range of the pistol the man was using.
At the man's trial, what verdict should the jury return?

choices.A: Guilty of attempted murder, because a reasonable person would not have been aware of the limited range of the pistol.
choices.B: Guilty of attempted murder, because the man was not aware of the limited range of his pistol.
choices.C: Not guilty of attempted murder, but guilty of assault.
choices.D: Not guilty of attempted murder or any lesser included offense, because it was impossible for the man to have killed his coworker.

questions.explanation:
A defendant is guilty of attempt if he/she:

  • had the specific intent to commit a crime (eg, murder)
  • performed an act in furtherance of the target crime but
  • did not complete it.

In most jurisdictions, an act is a substantial step taken toward the completion of the target crime that exceeds mere preparation and strongly corroborates criminal intent. Once this occurs, the defendant can be convicted of attempt even if it was factually impossible to complete the target crime.

Here, the man wanted to kill his coworker (intent to commit murder) and fired five shots at him with a pistol. None of the shots came anywhere close to the coworker because he was well out of the pistol's range (factual impossibility). But since the man was not aware of the pistol's limited range, he acted with the intent to kill the coworker—and took a substantial step toward murder by pulling the trigger (overt act). Therefore, the jury should find him guilty of attempted murder.

(Choice A) There is no reasonable person standard for attempt. Therefore, the man can be guilty of attempt even if a reasonable person would not have been aware of the pistol's limited range.

(Choice C) Assault is (1) an attempted battery or (2) conduct that intentionally puts the victim in reasonable apprehension of imminent bodily harm. Here, the man may have committed assault when he shot at the coworker. But since the man intended to kill his coworker, the jury should find the man guilty of the greater offense of attempted murder.

(Choice D) It was impossible for the man to kill his coworker under the circumstances since the coworker was well out of the pistol's range. But factual impossibility is never a defense to attempt.

📌 Educational Objective

Attempt requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to commit a crime and performed an act (ie, substantial step) in furtherance of that crime. A defendant can be convicted even if it was factually impossible for the target crime to be committed.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子想要杀死他的同事，因为他相信该同事与他的妻子有染。一天清晨，该男子携带手枪，蹲伏在公园山坡的灌木丛后，俯瞰着他同事经常慢跑的一条小路。然而，在那个早晨，该男子看到他的同事在约半英里外的另一条小路上慢跑。尽管如此，该男子还是向其同事开了五枪。由于同事远在该男子所使用手枪的射程之外，这五枪无一命中或接近该同事。

在该男子的审判中，陪审团应作出何种裁决？

zh-choices.A: 犯谋杀未遂罪，因为一个理性人不会意识到手枪的射程有限。
zh-choices.B: 犯谋杀未遂罪，因为该男子没有意识到他手枪的射程有限。
zh-choices.C: 不构成谋杀未遂罪，但构成攻击罪。
zh-choices.D: 不构成谋杀未遂罪或任何轻于此罪之罪，因为该男子不可能杀死他的同事。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Attempt & Impossibility

⚖️ 核心考点：事实不能 (Factual Impossibility)

在刑法中，如果被告具有实施犯罪的特定意图 (Specific Intent)，并且采取了实质性步骤 (Substantial Step)，即使由于被告未知的客观事实原因导致犯罪无法完成，他仍然构成未遂罪 (Attempt)。

关键规则：事实不能 (Factual Impossibility) 不是未遂罪的抗辩理由。

🔍 案情逻辑分析

本案中，被告的行为完全符合未遂罪的构成要件：

  • 意图 (Intent)： 他明确想要杀死同事（Specific intent to kill）。
  • 行为 (Act)： 他瞄准并扣动了扳机开了五枪（Overt act / Substantial step）。
  • 结果 (Result)： 没打中，因为距离太远（超出射程）。

这是一个典型的事实不能 (Factual Impossibility) 案例。虽然客观上这把枪打不到半英里外，但被告主观上不知道这一点。如果情况如他所想（枪的射程足够），犯罪就会发生。

✅ 正确答案解析
选项 B 正确

"Guilty of attempted murder, because the man was not aware of the limited range of his pistol."

解析：这句话精准地指出了被告的主观状态。因为他不知道射程有限（事实错误），他仍然保有杀人的意图并付诸实施。既然事实不能不是抗辩理由，他必须承担未遂责任。

❌ 错误选项陷阱
选项 A 错误

陷阱：理性人标准 (Reasonable Person)

未遂罪是特定意图犯罪 (Specific Intent Crime)，关注的是被告实际在想什么，而不是一个“理性人”会怎么想。即使一个理性人知道手枪打不了半英里，只要这个被告不知道并试图杀人，他就构成未遂。

选项 D 错误

陷阱：不可能抗辩 (Impossibility Defense)

该选项声称“因为不可能杀死，所以无罪”。这是错误的法律陈述。只有法律不能 (Legal Impossibility)（即被告想做的事在法律上根本不算犯罪）才是抗辩理由。本案是事实不能，不能脱罪。

💡 MBE 提分技巧：
遇到“未遂 (Attempt)”题目时，问自己两个问题：
  1. 他想犯罪吗？(Specific Intent)
  2. 他动手了吗？(Substantial Step)
如果答案都是 YES，但因为客观原因（如枪没子弹、口袋是空的、距离太远）失败了，这就是事实不能，必须判有罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:
CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.
CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.
CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.
CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes let his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.
A college student purchased narcotics from a man whom the student believed to be a drug dealer but who was in fact an undercover police agent. The student has been charged as an accomplice to the sale of narcotics.
Should the student be convicted or acquitted of this crime?

choices.A: Convicted on the authority of Case A.
choices.B: Convicted on the authority of Case B.
choices.C: Acquitted on the authority of Case C.
choices.D: Acquitted on the authority of Case D.

questions.explanation:
Exclusions from accomplice liability
Member of
protected class		 Members of class criminal statute was designed to protect are immune from liability (eg, statutory rape)
Exempted
necessary party		 When crime requires multiple participants but criminal statute only imposes liability on one, others are immune from liability (eg, sale of narcotics)
Withdrawal No liability if accomplice voluntarily withdraws before crime becomes unstoppable by:
  • repudiating encouragement
  • undoing or neutralizing assistance
  • notifying authorities or otherwise preventing crime

A defendant can be convicted as an accomplice to a crime if he/she intentionally helped or encouraged the principal before or during the crime with the specific intent that the principal complete that crime. But a person who would otherwise be an accomplice is exempt from liability when:

  • the crime requires more than one participant (eg, bribery requires an offeror and recipient) but
  • the criminal statute only imposes liability on one participant (eg, only the recipient—not the offeror).

Here, a student purchased drugs and was charged as an accomplice to the sale of narcotics—an offense that requires two participants (a seller and a purchaser). But only a seller can be liable for the sale of narcotics, just as only an official can be liable for taking a bribe in Case C. Therefore, the student is exempt from accomplice liability and should be acquitted of this crime.

(Choice A) In Case A, a hardware store owner (accomplice) sold a device that helped speeders (principals) avoid detection. He was not exempt from accomplice liability since—unlike here—the law did not limit criminal liability to a certain participant.

(Choice B) Case B addresses the defendant's principal liability for a burglary carried out by an innocent agent (the friend)—a person who was tricked or forced into committing a criminal act. But this case is inapplicable here because the student was not a principal to the unlawful sale of narcotics—he was merely the buyer.

(Choice D) As Case D shows, mere knowledge that the principal intends to use a person's aid—particularly aid involving the sale of goods or services—to commit a crime does not make that person an accomplice. An accomplice must have some greater interest in the commission of that crime (eg, selling at a higher price). Since the student purchased drugs, this authority does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

When a crime requires at least two participants but the criminal statute only imposes liability on one participant, all other participants are exempt from accomplice liability.

应依据 Case C 的判例宣告无罪 (Acquitted)。

核心法律原则：被豁免的必要参与方

本题考查的是从犯责任中的一个重要例外：Exempted Necessary Party（被豁免的必要参与方）。

如果一项犯罪在定义上必然需要两个人的参与（例如：销售毒品需要买方和卖方，行贿需要行贿人和受贿人），但法律条文仅惩罚其中一方，那么另一方通常不能被指控为该罪行的从犯 (Accomplice)。

这反映了立法意图 (Legislative Intent)：立法者选择不惩罚另一方，或者通过其他特定的法规来惩罚另一方（例如惩罚“持有”而非“协助销售”）。

判例逻辑映射

解题的关键在于找到题目事实与给定判例之间的法律逻辑对应关系。

比较项 Case C (判例) 本案事实
罪行性质 贿赂 (Bribery)
需行贿方与受贿方		 销售毒品 (Sale of Narcotics)
需卖方与买方
法律条文 禁止收受贿赂
(针对受贿官员)		 禁止销售毒品
(针对卖家)
被告角色 行贿人 (Giver)
交易的必要参与方		 买家 (Purchaser)
交易的必要参与方
结论 不构成从犯 不构成从犯

正如 Case C 中行贿人不能作为“受贿罪”的从犯一样，本案中买毒品的学生也不能作为“贩毒罪”的从犯。虽然他购买的行为确实“帮助”了销售的完成，但他属于受立法保护或豁免的必要参与方。

为什么其他判例不适用？

Case A 通用协助 (General Aid)：
五金店主卖雷达探测器。超速并不必然需要雷达探测器，店主只是外部协助者，不属于“必要参与方”。因此该判例不适用。

Case B 无辜代理人 (Innocent Agent)：
被告利用不知情的朋友实施盗窃。这是关于主犯 (Principal) 利用他人作为工具的责任，而本案学生是与毒贩进行交易，并非利用毒贩作为无辜工具。

Case D 知情与意图 (Knowledge vs. Intent)：
旅店老板知情但照常收费。这涉及仅仅“知情”是否足以构成协助意图的问题。虽然这也是从犯责任的考点，但 Case C 提供了更直接、更精准的“必要参与方”豁免依据。

💡 MBE 考试技巧：
当题目给出具体的“Decisional Law”（判例法）时，你的任务不是应用通用的刑法规则，而是严格类比题目给出的规则。

寻找事实模式 (Fact Pattern) 最接近的判例。本题中，“双向交易罪行”且“只惩罚一方”的特征，使得 Case C 成为唯一的完美对应。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man asked his girlfriend to lend him something he could use to break into his neighbor's padlocked storage shed in order to steal a lawn mower. She handed him a crowbar. He took the crowbar but then found a bolt cutter that the neighbor had left outside the shed. Using the bolt cutter, he cut the padlock on the shed and took the mower, which he then used to mow his girlfriend's lawn. She was surprised and pleased by this gesture.
Burglary in the jurisdiction applies to any structure or building, and there is no nighttime element. The girlfriend has been charged as an accomplice to burglary and larceny.
Of which crimes, if any, is she guilty?

choices.A: Burglary and larceny.
choices.B: Burglary, but not larceny, because she intended to assist only in the breaking.
choices.C: Larceny, but not burglary, because she provided no actual assistance to the breaking but received a benefit from the larceny.
choices.D: Neither burglary nor larceny, because she provided no actual assistance.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
(modern & majority approach)
Party Definition Liability
Principal
  • Commits criminal act with requisite mens rea or
  • Tricks or forces another (ie, innocent agent) to commit criminal act
 Liable for resulting crime
Accomplice
  • Aids or encourages principal before or during crime with intent that principal commit crime
 Liable to same extent as principal
Accessory
after the fact
  • Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction
 Liable for independent crime (not principal's)

Accomplice liability arises when a person:

  • intentionally aids or encourages another (ie, the principal) before or during a crime
  • with the specific intent that the encouraged crime be completed.

Slight aid or encouragement will suffice, even when such assistance is not necessary to complete the crime. An accomplice is liable to the same extent as the principal for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

This jurisdiction (like most others) defines burglary as the unlawful entry of a structure or building with the intent to commit a crime (eg, larceny) therein. Therefore, the girlfriend aided the man with the intent that he commit both burglary and larceny by breaking into the neighbor's shed and stealing a lawn mower (Choices B & C). Therefore, the girlfriend is guilty of both burglary and larceny.

(Choice D) Although the man ultimately used a bolt cutter instead of the girlfriend's crowbar to accomplish the burglary and larceny, she still provided the aid necessary to be guilty as an accomplice. This is because only slight aid or encouragement is required for accomplice liability.

📌 Educational Objective

Accomplice liability is imposed when a person provides even slight aid or encouragement to the principal with the specific intent that the encouraged crime be completed—even when that assistance is not necessary to complete the crime.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子要求其女友借他一件东西，用来闯入邻居上了锁的储物棚，以便偷走一台割草机。她给了他一根撬棍。他拿了撬棍，但随后发现了一把邻居遗落在棚外的断线钳。他用断线钳剪断了棚上的挂锁，拿走了割草机，并用它为女友修剪了草坪。她对这一举动感到惊喜和高兴。

在该司法管辖区，入室犯法罪适用于任何构筑物或建筑物，且没有夜间要素。该女友被指控为入室犯法罪和盗窃罪的共犯。

如果构成犯罪，她犯了哪些罪？

zh-choices.A: 入室犯法罪和盗窃罪。
zh-choices.B: 入室犯法罪，但不构成盗窃罪，因为她只意图协助闯入行为。
zh-choices.C: 盗窃罪，但不构成入室犯法罪，因为她没有为闯入行为提供实际帮助，但从盗窃行为中获益。
zh-choices.D: 既不构成入室犯法罪，也不构成盗窃罪，因为她没有提供实际帮助。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

共犯责任与无效帮助
Accomplice Liability & Ineffective Aid

✅ 正确答案：A

女友构成入室犯法罪 (Burglary) 和 盗窃罪 (Larceny)。

⚖️ 核心考点：共犯责任

要成为共犯 (Accomplice)，被告必须满足两个条件：

  1. 犯罪意图 (Mens Rea)： 具有协助主犯的意图，并希望犯罪得逞 (Specific Intent)。
  2. 犯罪行为 (Actus Reus)： 在犯罪前或犯罪中提供了帮助、鼓励或建议。
1. 关键争议点：未被使用的工具

这是本题最大的陷阱。女友提供了撬棍 (Crowbar)，但主犯实际上使用的是断线钳 (Bolt cutter)。

在普通法和MBE考试规则中，共犯的帮助不需要是犯罪发生的“必要条件” (But-for cause)。

只要提供了帮助（哪怕是微小的帮助，Slight aid），或者进行了鼓励，共犯责任即成立。女友递给男友撬棍的行为本身就是一种物质上的支持和心理上的鼓励 (Encouragement)，即便该工具最终未被使用，她的共犯责任依然无法免除。

2. 责任范围 (Scope of Liability)

共犯不仅对“目标犯罪”负责，还对犯罪过程中所有自然且可能 (Natural and Probable) 的后果负责。

  • 入室犯法罪 (Burglary)： 闯入棚屋是目标行为。
  • 盗窃罪 (Larceny)： 偷割草机是闯入的目的，也是直接后果。

因此，她对这两项罪名均负有责任。

🚫 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 D (无罪)： 错误地认为“没有提供实际帮助（因为工具没用上）”就不构成犯罪。法律看重的是“提供帮助的意图和行为”，而非帮助的实际效果。
选项 B (仅Burglary)： 错误。她借工具的目的是为了让他“偷割草机”，因此她对盗窃也有特定的意图。
选项 C (仅Larceny)： 错误。没有入室行为就无法拿到割草机，两者是紧密联系的。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧

看到“共犯提供帮助但未成功”或“工具未被使用”的情节时，请记住：

Attempt to aid is enough. (试图帮助即足矣)

只要有特定意图 (Specific Intent) 加上任何形式的鼓励或支持，哪怕是精神上的支持 (Psychological support)，共犯责任即锁定。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A drug dealer agreed with another individual to purchase heroin from the individual in order to sell it on a city street corner. Unbeknownst to the drug dealer, the other individual was an undercover police officer whose only purpose was to arrest distributors of drugs. The drug dealer made a down payment for the heroin and agreed to pay the remainder after he sold it on the street. As soon as the undercover officer handed over the heroin, other officers moved in and arrested the dealer.
The jurisdiction follows the common law approach to conspiracy.
Could the dealer properly be convicted of conspiring to distribute drugs?

choices.A: No, because there was no overt act.
choices.B: No, because there was no plurality of agreement.
choices.C: Yes, because neither an overt act nor plurality of agreement is required at common law.
choices.D: Yes, because the dealer believed that all the elements of conspiracy were present and cannot take advantage of a mistake of fact or law.

questions.explanation:
Common-law conspiracy

Guilty mind
Guilty mind
Plurality of agreement
= conspiracy
Feigned
agreement
Guilty mind
No plurality of agreement
≠ conspiracy

Common law conspiracy is (1) an agreement between two or more persons to commit a crime that is (2) entered with the specific intent to accomplish that crime. This requires proof of at least two guilty minds (ie, plurality of agreement). As a result, a defendant cannot be convicted of this crime if the other alleged conspirators feigned agreement.

Here, the drug dealer and another individual agreed to purchase and distribute heroin. But since that individual was an undercover police officer whose only purpose was to arrest drug distributors (not to commit a crime), there was no plurality of agreement. As a result, the dealer cannot properly be convicted of conspiracy in this common law jurisdiction.

(Choices A & C) Although common law conspiracy requires plurality of agreement, it does not require an overt act—discernible evidence that a conspiracy is at work (eg, the dealer's payment for drugs).

(Choice D) Mistake of law is rarely a defense to any crime. And mistake of fact is only a defense to conspiracy if that honest mistake negates the specific intent to commit a crime. Here, the dealer's mistaken belief that all elements of conspiracy were present would support that intent. But these defenses need not be considered since no conspiracy occurred.

📌 Educational Objective

Common law conspiracy requires proof of at least two guilty minds (ie, plurality of agreement), so the defendant cannot be convicted of conspiring with persons who feigned agreement.
questions.zh-question:
一名毒贩与另一个人约定，从其手中购买海洛因，以便在城市街角贩卖。该毒贩不知道的是，另一个人是一名卧底警察，其唯一目的是逮捕毒品分销者。毒贩为海洛因支付了首付款，并同意在街上售出后再支付余款。卧底警察一交出海洛因，其他警察便上前逮捕了该毒贩。

该司法管辖区遵循普通法中对共谋罪的规定。

该毒贩是否可以被正当判定犯有共谋分销毒品罪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为没有公开行为。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为没有合意的多数性。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为在普通法中，既不需要公开行为，也不需要合意的多数性。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为毒贩相信共谋罪的所有要素都已具备，且不能利用事实错误或法律错误为自己辩护。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Inchoate Crimes: Conspiracy
(未遂犯罪：共谋罪)
⚖️ 核心法则：双务原则 (Bilateral Theory)

本题明确指出该司法管辖区遵循普通法 (Common Law)。在普通法下，共谋罪必须满足合意的多数性 (Plurality of Agreement)。

这意味着必须有两个或两个以上的人真正打算实施犯罪。如果其中一方只是假装同意（如卧底警察），则不存在法律意义上的“协议”。

🕵️ 案情逻辑分析

1. 毒贩 (Defendant):
具有犯罪意图 (Guilty Mind)，意图购买并分销海洛因。

2. 卧底警察 (Undercover Officer):
虽然表面上同意，但内心没有犯罪意图。其目的是执法而非犯罪。这被称为 Feigned Agreement（假意合谋）。

3. 结论:
1个真正的犯罪意图 + 0个真正的犯罪意图 = 1个犯罪意图。
普通法共谋罪要求至少 2个。因此，共谋罪不成立。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (公开行为)
错误。普通法上的共谋罪不需要公开行为 (Overt Act)。只要达成协议即构成犯罪。即便需要，毒贩付款也是公开行为。
选项 B (正确答案)
正确。因为缺乏“合意的多数性”，即没有两个“Guilty Minds”。

关于选项 D (事实/法律错误):
毒贩确实“以为”自己在共谋，但这属于法律上的不可能 (Legal Impossibility)。因为对方是警察，法律上根本无法形成普通法定义的共谋。被告的主观信念不能弥补客观要素（第二个共谋者）的缺失。

💡 MBE 考试陷阱提示

务必看清题目适用的法律是 Common Law 还是 Model Penal Code (MPC)。

  • Common Law: 必须两人以上真合谋 (Bilateral)。卧底警察 = 无罪。
  • MPC / Modern Statutes: 采用单务原则 (Unilateral Theory)。只要被告认为自己在与他人共谋，即便对方是卧底，被告仍有罪。

本题若改为 MPC 规则，答案将完全相反！

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man and a woman agreed that the woman would rob a bank and that the man would steal a car beforehand for the woman to use as a getaway vehicle. The man stole a car and parked it two blocks from the bank. He left the car key under the floor mat with a note saying that he wanted nothing more to do with the scheme. The next day, the woman robbed the bank and ran to the spot where the man had said he would leave the stolen car. She then escaped in the car and disappeared. She never shared any of the money with the man.
In a jurisdiction that has adopted the bilateral requirement for conspiracy, can the man properly be convicted of conspiring with the woman to rob the bank?

choices.A: No, because the man received no benefit from the robbery.
choices.B: No, because the man withdrew from the conspiracy.
choices.C: Yes, because the robbery was successful due in part to the man's actions.
choices.D: Yes, because there was an agreement to rob the bank and an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.

Agreement Overt act
Majority view
(modern & MPC) 		Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement At least one conspirator must commit overt act
Minority view
(common law) 		Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement Not required
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Conspiracy, at its core, is an agreement between two or more persons to commit a crime. Proof of an agreement depends on whether the prosecuting jurisdiction follows either:

  • the bilateral approach (minority rule) – requires proof that two or more persons entered the agreement with the specific intent to commit the target crime, so the defendant must be acquitted if other participants feigned agreement or
  • the unilateral approach (majority rule) – requires proof that the defendant entered the agreement with the specific intent to commit the target crime, so the defendant can be convicted even if other participants feigned agreement.

And most jurisdictions also require proof that at least one of the conspirators committed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy.

Here, there is proof of two guilty minds since the man and the woman agreed and specifically intended to rob a bank by having (1) the man steal a getaway vehicle and (2) the woman rob the bank. And they both committed overt acts in furtherance of their agreement when he stole the getaway car and she robbed the bank. As a result, the man can be convicted of conspiracy in this bilateral-approach jurisdiction (and any other jurisdiction).

(Choice A) A conspirator need not benefit from the target crime to be convicted of conspiracy.

(Choice B) A defendant can withdraw from a conspiracy before it is completed. But since the man attempted to withdraw after the conspiracy was completed—ie, after an agreement was formed and, if required, an overt act occurred—withdrawal is no defense.

(Choice C) The bank robbery was successful due in part to the man's overt act—stealing the getaway car. But he could be convicted even if the overt act had been completed by another conspirator or if the robbery had failed.

📌 Educational Objective

The bilateral approach to conspiracy (minority rule) requires proof that two or more persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime. But the unilateral approach (majority rule) only requires proof that the defendant entered an agreement with such intent.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子和一名女子约定，女子去抢劫一家银行，男子事先偷一辆车供女子用作逃跑车辆。该男子偷了一辆车，并将其停在离银行两个街区远的地方。他把车钥匙留在脚垫下，并附上一张纸条，说他不想再与该计划有任何瓜葛。第二天，该女子抢劫了银行，并跑到该男子说好会留下被盗车辆的地点。随后，她驾车逃离并消失了。她从未与该男子分享任何赃款。

在一个采纳共谋罪双边要求的司法管辖区内，该男子是否可以因与该女子共谋抢劫银行而被适当定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为该男子没有从抢劫中获得任何利益。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该男子退出了共谋。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为抢劫的成功部分归因于该男子的行为。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为存在抢劫银行的协议和为推进该协议而实施的公开行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 刑法考点解析

Criminal Law: Conspiracy
⚖️ 核心考点：共谋罪 (Conspiracy)

共谋罪的成立通常需要满足两个要素：

  1. 两人或多人达成实施犯罪的协议 (Agreement)。
  2. 为推进该协议而实施的公开行为 (Overt Act)（大多数司法管辖区及本题要求）。

双边要求 (Bilateral Requirement)：
普通法（Common Law）遵循双边原则，要求至少有两人真正意图达成协议。如果一方是假装同意（如卧底警察），则另一方不能被判共谋罪。

🕵️ 案情关键点分析

  • 协议达成：男子和女子都同意抢劫银行（Man and woman agreed）。这里没有卧底，两人都是真心实意的（满足双边要求）。
  • 公开行为：男子偷了一辆车并停在指定位置。这是一个实质性的步骤（Overt Act）。
  • 试图退出：男子在偷车后留下了字条表示想退出。

✅ 正确答案解析

选项 D 正确

理由：共谋罪是一种"即成犯"。一旦达成协议并实施了公开行为（偷车），共谋罪就已经既遂 (Completed)。

本题中，存在明确的协议，且男子实施了公开行为（偷车）。因此，共谋罪的构成要件已全部满足。

❌ 常见陷阱与错误选项

选项 B 错误（关于退出/Withdrawal）

这是本题最大的干扰项。考生常混淆"退出共谋"的法律后果。

  • 规则：一旦共谋罪既遂（协议+公开行为），被告无法通过事后退出来撤销共谋罪本身的指控。
  • 例外：有效的退出（Withdrawal）通常只能作为后续犯罪（如本案中的抢劫罪）的抗辩理由，而不能免除共谋罪本身的责任。
  • 本案事实：即便作为后续犯罪的抗辩，男子的退出也是无效的。他只是留了张纸条，没有成功阻止犯罪（Thwart the crime）或及时通知警方。
选项 A 错误（关于利益）

共谋罪不要求被告从犯罪中获利。未分得赃款不影响定罪。

选项 C 错误（关于成功）

虽然男子的行为确实帮助了抢劫，但共谋罪的定罪依据是"协议"本身，而不是目标犯罪是否成功。即使抢劫失败，共谋罪依然成立。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到 "Withdrawal"（退出） 时要警惕：

  1. 时间点：是在公开行为发生前还是发生后？（发生后共谋罪已成立）。
  2. 对象：退出是针对"共谋罪"本身（通常无效），还是针对"目标犯罪"（可能有效，但要求很高，通常需要阻止犯罪发生）。
  3. 题目条件：注意题目是否提及 "Bilateral"（双边）或 "Unilateral"（单边/MPC）。本题强调双边，意在确认两人都有犯罪意图，排除了"假装同意"的情况。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A girl told an 18-year-old boy she would like to have sexual intercourse with him and that he should come to her apartment that night at 7 p.m. After the boy arrived, he and the girl went into the bedroom. As the boy started to remove the girl's blouse, she said she had changed her mind. The boy tried to convince her to have intercourse with him, but after ten minutes of her sustained refusals, he left the apartment. Unknown to the boy, the girl was 15 years old. Because she appeared to be older, the boy believed her to be about 18 years old.
A statute in the jurisdiction provides: "A person commits rape in the second degree if he has sexual intercourse with a girl, not his wife, who is under the age of 16 years."
If the boy is charged with attempting to violate this statute, what is the proper verdict?

choices.A: Guilty, because he persisted after she told him she had changed her mind.
choices.B: Guilty, because no mental state is required as to the element of age.
choices.C: Not guilty, because he did not intend to have intercourse with a girl under the age of 16.
choices.D: Not guilty, because he reasonably believed she had consented and voluntarily withdrew after she told him she had changed her mind.

questions.explanation:
Types of mens rea
Specific intent
(all attempted crimes)
General intent
(battery, rape)
Strict liability
(sale to minor, statutory rape)
Intentional Purposely or knowingly causes
particular result
Reckless Consciously disregards substantial &
unjustifiable risk
Criminally Negligent Grossly deviates from
standard of reasonable care
No mens rea No showing of
fault required

Attempt is an inchoate crime that occurs when the defendant:

  • has the specific intent to commit a crime
  • performs an act in furtherance of the intended crime but
  • does not complete it.

Therefore, an attempt to violate this jurisdiction's criminal statute requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to have sexual intercourse with a girl under 16 years of age. This is true even when the target crime (statutory rape) is a strict liability offense that does not require proof of a particular mental state as to the element of age (Choice B).

Here, the boy tried to convince the 15-year-old girl to have sexual intercourse with him. But he did not intend to have intercourse with a girl under the age of 16 since the girl appeared to be older and the boy believed her to be about 18 years old. As a result, he should be found not guilty of attempting to violate the statute.

(Choice A) Had the boy possessed the requisite intent for attempt, his persistent efforts to convince the girl to have intercourse with him may have satisfied the act requirement. But since the boy lacked such intent, he should not be convicted of attempt.

(Choice D) Consent is not an element of statutory rape or attempt, so the boy's reasonable belief that the girl had consented is irrelevant. And since attempt is complete once the act is committed, abandonment is no defense. Therefore, the fact that the boy voluntarily left the girl's apartment after she changed her mind would not absolve him of liability.

📌 Educational Objective

Attempt always requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to commit a crime—even if the target crime does not require specific intent (eg, statutory rape).
questions.zh-question:
一名女孩告诉一名18岁男孩，她想与他发生性关系，并让他当晚7点来她的公寓。男孩到达后，他和女孩进入了卧室。当男孩开始脱女孩的上衣时，她表示改变了主意。男孩试图说服她与自己发生性关系，但在她持续拒绝十分钟后，他离开了公寓。男孩不知道的是，该女孩年仅15岁。因为她看起来更年长，男孩相信她大约18岁。

该司法管辖区的一项法规规定：“与非其妻的未满16岁女孩发生性关系者，构成二级强奸罪。”

如果该男孩被指控试图违反此法规，何为恰当的裁决？

zh-choices.A: 有罪，因为在女孩表示改变主意后他仍坚持不懈。
zh-choices.B: 有罪，因为对于年龄这一犯罪构成要件，法律不要求行为人具有特定的犯罪心理状态。
zh-choices.C: 无罪，因为他无意与未满16岁的女孩发生性关系。
zh-choices.D: 无罪，因为他合理地相信她已同意，并在她表示改变主意后自愿中止了行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Attempt & Strict Liability
⚖️ 核心法则 (The Golden Rule) 未遂罪 (Attempt) 永远是特定意图犯罪 (Specific Intent Crime)，即使其试图实施的目标罪行是严格责任犯罪 (Strict Liability Crime)。
✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 C)

本题的正确答案是 C。要理解这一点，必须区分“既遂犯”与“未遂犯”对心理状态 (Mens Rea) 的不同要求。

  • 目标罪行 (Target Crime)： 法定强奸罪 (Statutory Rape)。通常这是一个严格责任犯罪，意味着如果行为既遂，被告人不知道受害者未成年这一事实不能作为抗辩理由。
  • 被控罪行 (Charged Crime)： 试图违反该法规 (Attempting to violate...)。

法律逻辑推演：

未遂罪 (Attempt) 要求被告人具有实施犯罪行为的特定意图 (Specific Intent)。这意味着被告人必须主观上“想要”实现犯罪的所有构成要件。

在本案中，为了构成“法定强奸未遂”，检方必须证明男孩具体意图与一名未满16岁的女孩发生性关系。

事实应用：
题目明确指出男孩“相信她大约18岁”。因此，他缺乏与未满16岁女孩发生性关系的特定意图。因为缺乏这一必要的心理状态 (Mens Rea)，他不能被判未遂罪。

⚠️ 常见陷阱 (为什么 B 是错的)

选项 B 是最强的干扰项，也是 MBE 考试中经典的“严格责任陷阱”。

考生常犯错误：
认为既然法定强奸是严格责任犯罪（不需要意图），那么其未遂罪也不需要意图。

纠正： 这是一个法律上的悖论。虽然你可能因“意外”与未成年人发生性关系而构成既遂犯（严格责任），但你不可能“意外”地试图去犯这个罪。未遂本质上要求你有目的性地去追求那个非法的后果。

❌ 其他选项排除
  • 选项 A (坚持不懈)： 行为 (Actus Reus) 再多，如果没有对应的犯罪意图 (Mens Rea)，也不能构成未遂罪。
  • 选项 D (同意与中止)：
    1. 同意 (Consent) 对法定强奸无效。
    2. 中止 (Abandonment/Withdrawal)：一旦实施了明显的越界行为 (Overt Act)，普通法通常不接受中止作为抗辩。
    该选项错误的原因在于它讨论了抗辩理由，而本案在构成要件阶段（意图）就已经不成立了。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A hair technician agreed to implant synthetic hair into the scalp of her customer. The customer explained to the hair technician that he often broke into people's houses to take jewelry and that he wanted to avoid leaving his own hair at the scene as incriminating evidence. The technician, knowing that a great deal of the synthetic hair would fall out due to implant rejection, that the strands would still have the customer's DNA at the root, and that the procedure would be no help at all in hiding forensic evidence, said nothing. The technician completed the procedure and charged her regular hourly rate. The next night, the customer broke into a house and stole a diamond ring. He later was convicted of burglary based on hair evidence he left behind.
The jurisdiction follows the Model Penal Code rule regarding accomplice liability.
Should the hair technician be convicted of burglary as an accomplice?

choices.A: No, because she did not break into the house and steal the ring.
choices.B: No, because she did not have the requisite intent for accomplice liability.
choices.C: Yes, because she failed to notify legal authorities in a timely manner.
choices.D: Yes, because she knew that the customer broke into houses regularly.

questions.explanation:
Parties to a crime
Modern view Common law Definition Liability
Principal Principal
(first degree)		 Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act Target &
foreseeable
crimes
Accomplice Principal
(second degree)		 Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
before the fact*		 Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime
Accessory
after the fact		 Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction Independent
crime
*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

An accomplice (i.e., accessory) to a crime is fully liable for the principal's conduct. But in most jurisdictions and under the Model Penal Code, accomplice liability will only be imposed if the accomplice has a dual intent:

  • the specific intent to aid or encourage the principal before or during the crime and
  • the specific intent that the principal commit the crime.

Mere knowledge that another person intends to commit a crime is not enough to impose accomplice liability.

Here, the hair technician implanted synthetic hair into her customer's scalp. After the procedure, the customer was convicted of burglary for breaking into a house and stealing a ring. But even though the hair technician knew that the customer broke into houses regularly, there is no indication that she had the specific intent to aid or encourage the customer or the specific intent that he commit the crime (Choice D).

And since the hair technician did not have the requisite intent for accomplice liability, she should not be convicted of burglary as an accomplice.

(Choice A) The fact that the hair technician did not break into the house and steal the ring means that she cannot be convicted of burglary as a principal. But she could have been convicted as an accomplice had she possessed the requisite intent (not seen here).

(Choice C) The hair technician had no duty to notify legal authorities in a timely manner that the customer often broke into people's houses to take jewelry. Therefore, she cannot be convicted of burglary as an accomplice for failing to do so.

📌 Educational Objective

In most jurisdictions and under the Model Penal Code, a conviction based on accomplice liability requires proof that a person (1) intentionally aided or encouraged the principal before or during the crime and (2) intended that the principal commit the crime. Mere knowledge that another person intends to commit a crime is not enough.

📚 References
  • Model Penal Code § 2.06(3) (defining accomplice liability).
questions.zh-question: 一名发型师同意为她的顾客植入合成头发。顾客向发型师解释说，他经常闯入他人的房屋盗窃珠宝，并希望避免在现场留下自己的头发作为定罪证据。该发型师知道大量合成头发会因植入排斥而脱落，发丝根部仍会带有顾客的DNA，并且该手术根本无助于隐藏法医证据，但她什么也没说。发型师完成了手术并收取了她常规的小时费率。第二天晚上，顾客闯入一所房屋并偷走了一枚钻戒。他后来因留下的头发证据而被判犯有入室盗窃罪 (burglary)。该司法管辖区遵循《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code) 关于共犯责任 (accomplice liability) 的规定。该发型师是否应作为共犯 (accomplice) 被判犯有入室盗窃罪 (burglary)？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为她没有闯入房屋并偷走戒指。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为她不具备共犯责任 (accomplice liability) 所需的意图。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

刑法与程序法: 未遂犯与共犯

正确答案: B

理由: 技师缺乏共犯责任所需的双重意图。

核心法律规则：共犯责任 (Model Penal Code)

共犯责任的构成要件

根据《模范刑法典》 (Model Penal Code, MPC)，一个人如果对主犯的行为负有共犯责任 (accomplice liability)，则其必须具备双重意图 (dual intent)：

  • 特定的意图：在犯罪发生之前或期间，帮助或鼓励 (aid or encourage) 主犯实施犯罪；并且
  • 特定的意图：主犯实施该犯罪 (commit the crime)。

仅仅知晓 (mere knowledge) 另一个人打算实施犯罪，不足以构成共犯责任。

概念对比：犯罪参与者分类

现代观点
(Modern view)		 普通法
(Common law)		 定义
(Definition)		 责任
(Liability)

案件事实与法律适用

本案中，发型技师为顾客植发，顾客告知技师他经常入室盗窃，并希望通过植发避免留下自己的头发作为证据。技师知道合成头发会脱落，且发根仍含有顾客的DNA，因此植发对隐藏法医证据毫无帮助。技师对此保持沉默，并完成了服务，收取了正常费用。随后，顾客实施了入室盗窃并被定罪。

  1. 技师的行为： 技师为顾客提供了植发服务，并知晓顾客的犯罪意图。
  2. 技师的知晓： 技师知道植发对隐藏证据无效，但未告知顾客。她也知道顾客经常入室盗窃。
  3. 共犯意图的缺失： 根据MPC，共犯责任要求技师具有双重意图：(1) 意图帮助或鼓励顾客实施盗窃，以及 (2) 意图顾客实施盗窃。
  4. 事实分析： 尽管技师知晓顾客的犯罪意图和其服务对隐藏证据的无效性，但没有证据表明她有积极的意图去帮助或鼓励顾客实施盗窃，也没有意图顾客去实施盗窃。她只是提供了常规的商业服务，即使她知道顾客的犯罪目的，且她的服务实际上对该目的毫无帮助。
  5. 结论： 技师的行为仅限于“知晓”顾客的犯罪意图，但缺乏MPC共犯责任所要求的“特定意图”去帮助或鼓励犯罪，以及“特定意图”去让犯罪发生。因此，她不应被判为盗窃罪的共犯。

MBE 考点陷阱：知晓与意图的混淆

MBE考试中常见的陷阱是混淆知晓 (knowledge) 与意图 (intent)。仅仅知道他人打算犯罪，或者知道自己的行为可能间接帮助犯罪，不足以构成共犯责任。共犯责任要求行为人具有积极的特定意图去帮助或鼓励犯罪，并且意图犯罪实际发生。如果缺乏这种双重意图，即使有知晓，也通常不构成共犯。

正确答案与干扰项排除

B. 否，因为她不具备共犯责任所需的意图。

正确。 根据《模范刑法典》(MPC)，共犯责任要求行为人具有双重意图：(1) 意图帮助或鼓励主犯实施犯罪，以及 (2) 意图主犯实施犯罪。本案中，技师虽然知道顾客的犯罪意图，但没有证据表明她有帮助或鼓励顾客实施盗窃的特定意图，也没有意图顾客实施盗窃。她只是提供了常规服务，即使知道该服务对犯罪目的无效。因此，她不具备共犯责任所需的意图。

A. 否，因为她没有闯入房屋并偷走戒指。

错误。 共犯责任不要求共犯亲自实施犯罪行为。共犯的责任在于其帮助、教唆或鼓励主犯实施犯罪的行为和意图。技师未亲自入室盗窃，这本身并不能排除其共犯责任，关键在于她是否具备共犯所需的意图。如果她具备了意图，即使没有亲自实施，也可能被视为共犯。

C. 是，因为她未能及时通知法律当局。

错误。 普通法下，公民通常没有法律义务向当局报告犯罪。虽然某些特殊关系（如医生-病人、律师-客户）可能存在保密义务，但本案中技师与顾客的关系不构成报告义务。因此，技师未报告顾客的犯罪意图，不构成共犯责任的基础。

D. 是，因为她知道顾客经常闯入房屋。

错误。 仅仅知道顾客经常入室盗窃，这只是知晓事实，而非共犯责任所需的特定意图。如核心法律规则所述，共犯责任要求行为人不仅知晓，更要意图帮助或鼓励犯罪，并意图犯罪发生。单纯的知晓不足以构成共犯责任。

考试技巧：共犯意图的严格性

在MBE考试中，共犯责任的“意图”要素是严格的。仅仅是知晓 (knowledge) 犯罪意图或提供可能被用于犯罪的常规服务 (routine service)，通常不足以构成共犯。考生必须寻找证据表明行为人具有积极的、双重的特定意图：即意图帮助或鼓励犯罪，并且意图犯罪实际发生。缺乏其中任何一个意图，都可能导致共犯责任不成立。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Nine gang members, including the gang leader, were indicted for the murder of a tenth gang member, who had become an informant. The gang leader pleaded guilty. At the trial of the other eight gang members, the state's evidence showed the following: The gang leader had announced a party to celebrate the release of a gang member from jail, but the party was not what it seemed. The gang leader had learned that the released gang member had earned his freedom by informing the authorities about the gang's criminal activities. The gang leader decided to use the party to let the other gang members see what happened to informants. He told no one about his plan. At the party, after everyone had consumed large amounts of liquor, the gang leader announced that the released gang member was an informant and stabbed him with a knife in front of the others. The eight other gang members watched and did nothing while the released gang member slowly bled to death. The jury found the eight gang members guilty of murder, and they appealed.
Should the appellate court uphold the convictions?

choices.A: No, because mere presence at the scene of a crime is insufficient to make a person an accomplice.
choices.B: No, because murder is a specific-intent crime, and there is insufficient evidence to show that the other gang members intended to kill.
choices.C: Yes, because the gang members made no effort to save the informant after he had been stabbed.
choices.D: Yes, because voluntary intoxication does not negate criminal responsibility.

*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

Accomplice liability extends to anyone who:

  • intentionally aided or encouraged the principal before or during a crime
  • with the specific intent that the crime be completed.

However, mere presence at the scene of a crime does not amount to aid or encouragement and is therefore insufficient to make a person an accomplice.

Here, the gang leader committed murder—an unlawful killing with malice aforethought—when he stabbed the informant to death. And though eight other gang members watched while the informant bled to death, they are not guilty of murder since they did nothing—and mere presence at a crime scene does not establish accomplice liability. As a result, the appellate court should not uphold the gang members' murder convictions.

(Choice B) Murder does not require specific intent to kill since other forms of malice aforethought (eg, depraved heart) will suffice. But regardless, the gang members are not responsible for the murder since they did not aid or encourage the gang leader's crime.

(Choice C) Criminal liability can only arise from a failure to act (ie, omission) if the defendant had a legal duty to act and could have reasonably done so. And since the gang members had no legal duty to save the informant, the fact that they made no effort to do so is irrelevant.

(Choice D) Voluntary intoxication does negate criminal responsibility for specific intent crimes when it prevents the defendant from forming the requisite mental state. But it does not matter whether the gang members were sober or intoxicated here since they were merely present (not responsible) for the murder.

📌 Educational Objective

An accomplice is someone who (1) intentionally aids or encourages the principal before or during a crime (2) with the specific intent that the crime be completed. But mere presence at the scene of a crime does not make a person an accomplice.

zh-choices.B: 不应，因为谋杀罪是特定意图犯罪，且没有足够证据表明其他帮派成员有杀人意图。
zh-choices.C: 应该，因为在线人被刺后，这些帮派成员没有做出任何努力去救他。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析
刑法：共犯责任

正确答案：A 不应维持判决，因为仅在犯罪现场不足以构成共犯 (Accomplice)。
核心考点：共犯责任与仅在现场
法律规则 (Black Letter Law)：
要承担共犯责任 (Accomplice Liability)，被告必须：
  1. 实际上帮助、教唆或鼓励了主犯 (Aid, Abet, or Encourage)；
  2. 具有特定的意图 (Intent)，即希望犯罪行为发生。
关键例外：仅仅出现在犯罪现场 (Mere Presence) 并不足以确立共犯责任，除非被告有法定的作为义务。
在本案中，虽然其他八名帮派成员在场并目睹了谋杀，但题目明确指出：
  • 头目没有告诉任何人他的计划（排除了共谋 Conspiracy）。
  • 其他成员只是“看着且什么都没做” (Watched and did nothing)。
由于他们没有提供任何实质性的帮助或鼓励（没有递刀、没有按住受害者、没有放风），仅仅是在场 (Presence) 和知情 (Knowledge) 并不构成犯罪。
干扰项辨析
选项 C 错误（关于不作为）：
这是最具迷惑性的选项。虽然他们在道德上令人谴责，但在法律上，刑事责任通常需要“作为” (Act)。
不作为 (Omission) 只有在被告负有法律义务 (Legal Duty) 时才构成犯罪（例如父母对子女、合同义务、或制造了危险源）。帮派成员之间没有法律上的救助义务，因此见死不救不构成犯罪。
选项 B 错误（关于意图）：
虽然缺乏意图确实可以作为辩护，但该选项的推理逻辑不如 A 直接。A 选项指出了更根本的问题：缺乏犯罪行为 (Actus Reus)。即使他们内心希望线人死（意图），如果没有实施帮助行为，也不能定罪。
选项 D 错误（关于醉酒）：
自愿醉酒 (Voluntary Intoxication) 是特定意图犯罪的辩护理由。但本题的关键在于他们根本没有实施犯罪行为（帮助或教唆），所以他们是否醉酒与本案结果无关。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 在处理共犯 (Accomplice) 题目时，请寻找“沉默的观察者”。

如果题目中的人物只是站在旁边看，没有点头示意、没有欢呼、没有放风，也没有事先的约定，那么无论他们的内心多么邪恶，根据美国刑法，这通常属于 Mere Presence，不承担刑事责任。
